justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: No RCT shows SFMA-guided treatment outperforms standard PT examination; supporting evidence is case reports, a pilot study, and one exploratory validity study with mixed findings.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applies broadly across outpatient orthopedic and sports caseloads since it is built for patients with pain, though it adds little in acute care, neuro, pelvic health, or geriatrics.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Confers no billing privileges or payer advantage; movement assessment is bundled into standard PT evaluation codes.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: The algorithmic top-tier-to-breakout structure systematizes whole-body examination, but the full breakout flowcharts are time-consuming to learn and apply initially.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Well recognized in sports medicine and performance-PT postings as preferred, essentially never required.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: The whole-body, regional-interdependence narrative resonates with active patients, but no published data link SFMA use to satisfaction.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Fits the cash-based sports/performance niche — movement assessments package naturally into athlete intake evaluations, and the FMS brand has consumer recognition in fitness circles.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Supports modest premium positioning for athlete-focused evaluations, but the contested evidence base and ubiquity among sports clinicians limit defensible uplift.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Recognizable branding helps marketing, but SFMA certification is common enough among sports-focused clinicians that it differentiates only in generalist markets.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: A standardized, trainable system that scales across staff and integrates with the broader FMS ecosystem for referral pipelines.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Steady demand in sports/performance segments; negligible pull in general orthopedic or Medicare-heavy markets.
justifications.business.efficiency: Low cost (~$799 per level, online and self-paced with CEU approval) and fast to complete — low payback threshold.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Viewed as a proprietary commercial product rather than an academic credential; the negative FMS predictive-validity literature has dented its scholarly standing.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: A genuine publishable literature exists (multiple IJSPT reliability studies) and open validity questions offer research opportunities, but the contested evidence cuts both ways.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: The structured algorithm is a useful pedagogical scaffold for teaching systematic movement examination; novice-reliability studies show students learn it quickly.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Reliability fair-to-moderate at best, SFMA-specific validity barely explored, and the parent FMS injury-prediction claims are contradicted by multiple meta-analyses.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Essentially never appears in faculty position requirements.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Cheap and quick relative to academic credentials, so time cost is trivial even if academic payoff is small.
